evals.name: agent-driven-demo
evals.prompt: Use the screen-record skill to describe the concrete workflow you would execute to record a short agent-driven UI demo, trim its setup, and preserve reproducible artifacts. Do not actually capture the screen in this eval.
evals.expected_output: A safe, ordered capture and editing workflow using the bundled managed recorder and preserving the raw source.
expectations: The workflow rehearses and prepares the application before recording.
The workflow uses the bundled start and stop commands rather than an unmanaged FFmpeg process.
The workflow coordinates application driving through computer-use tools.
The raw recording is preserved and trimming writes a new output.
The final file is probed or otherwise checked for duration, dimensions, and audio.

evals.name: side-by-side-captioned
evals.prompt: Use the screen-record skill to plan how to turn before.mp4 and after.mp4 into a 720p-high side-by-side comparison with captions.srt. Do not execute the commands; provide the exact bundled helper commands and output sequence.
evals.expected_output: An exact, reproducible two-stage side-by-side and subtitle workflow.
expectations: The response uses side-by-side with before.mp4 as left and after.mp4 as right.
The side-by-side command sets height to 720.
The response adds captions in a separate subtitles step.
Each stage writes to a new output path rather than overwriting an input.
The final output is inspected with the bundled probe command.

evals.name: local-narration
evals.prompt: Use the screen-record skill to add narration from narration.txt to demo.mp4 without sending text or media to a cloud service. Preserve the original video and explain the relevant voice-safety constraint.
evals.expected_output: A local platform-default narration and dubbing workflow that preserves source media, using SAPI on Windows and FFmpeg Flite elsewhere.
expectations: The response uses the bundled narrate command with narration.txt.
The response identifies SAPI as the default local narration engine on Windows.
The response uses the bundled dub command to create a new video.
The workflow is explicitly local and does not upload media or narration.
The response does not propose voice cloning or impersonation.
